properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING. Anthony, 2026-08-20, extending the flo2 chain-effect argument: *"if we can modularize reflow2 and know which functions that each module is supposed to perform, we can then do more encompassing testing (what are the edge cases, what are the failure modes, etc) that we might not be able to perform now."*

THE THIRD LEG OF ONE ARGUMENT. Modularization has now been argued for three distinct returns, and they are not the same return restated:
  1. SUBSTITUTABILITY — swap a module for another that meets the contract
  2. CHANGE PROPAGATION — follow a flo2-levied requirement along a chain (`fact:every-boundary-reaches-the-same-36-components-so-severability-is-not-computable`)
  3. DERIVABLE TESTING — this node

⭐ WHAT IS ALREADY THERE: function IS allocated. 138 ALLOCATED_TO edges put capabilities on components, so "which module performs which function" is largely answerable today.

🛑 WHAT IS NOT: the SHAPE of the function. `Capability.inputs` / `Capability.outputs` are declared in the schema and have NO typed tool to write them, NO instruction telling anyone to, and NO detector that notices their absence — the exact three-legged failure recorded in `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`. Edge cases are derived from the boundaries of an input domain and failure modes from what an output promises; with neither stated, both can only be imagined.

📌 AND IT MEETS THE VERIFICATION FINDING FROM THE SAME DAY: reflow2 holds 175 Verifications, 175 of kind `verification` and 0 of kind `validation`, 168 of method `test`. Every check asks whether the code matches the spec. Failure-mode work is the other question, and `Verification.method` already carries `analysis` and `inspection` — the FMEA-shaped methods — unused.

IDEAS: (a) make inputs/outputs writable and instructed, then ask for them where a Capability is allocated to a Component; (b) a detector for an allocated capability with no stated interface shape; (c) nothing — derive edge cases from the code as today, and accept that they are imagined rather than derived.

⚠️ COUNTER, and it is the standing one: `req:design-anything` keeps the vocabulary neutral, and "inputs and outputs" is comfortable for software and awkward for a building. Whether the shape generalises is unexamined.

⚠️ NOT COSTED, and nobody has asked for it. Recorded as the third return on a modularization nobody has scheduled.
properties.name: OPEN — the third thing modularization buys: if a module's function, inputs and outputs are stated, edge cases and failure modes become derivable rather than imagined
